about_page.subtitle: Establishing transparent indexing metrics for African scientific research.
about_page.mission_text1: Scholarly journals published in Africa frequently face structural barriers to inclusion in global indexing databases. AfriJournal Index was founded to bridge this gap, providing a free, high-standard indexing platform specifically designed for journals hosted across Africa.
about_page.mission_text2: Our platform evaluates quality guidelines fairly, using automation to verify ISSN standards, peer-review structures, publication frequency, and regional contributions to academic scholarship.
about_page.partner_text: In partnership with Kenya Projects Organization (KENPRO), we host a seed directory of verified, high-impact regional journals including ARJESS, JMBA, and IJEHS, ensuring local scientific inquiries are cataloged for global citation access.
about_page.pillar_open_text: Zero paywalls for journals and researchers to index and search African academic outputs.
about_page.pillar_metrics_text: Transparent impact calculation models designed to reflect African citation dynamics.
about_page.pillar_capacity_text: Automated compliance reports helping editorial teams elevate their peer review workflows.

methodology_page.desc: How we calculate standard citation impact factors and regional multipliers for African journals.
methodology_page.formula_desc: The African Journal Impact Factor (AJIF) is computed annually by tracking peer-reviewed articles and counting citations registered within the AfriJournal directory.
methodology_page.formula_num: Citations in 2025 to articles published in 2023-2024
methodology_page.regional_formula_desc: The regional score incorporates open access accessibility and cross-institutional African citations to reward scholarship that drives continental development.
methodology_page.criteria_1: Metadata Consistency: Verified active ISSN/eISSN status with official registries.
methodology_page.criteria_2: Open Peer-Review: Verified adherence to transparent editorial peer-review workflows.
methodology_page.criteria_3: Publishing Regularity: The journal must publish at least two issues annually without gap years.
methodology_page.criteria_4: Domain Security: Verified HTTPS encryption and active journal homepage.

items.a: AfriJournal Index (AJIF) is an open-access academic indexing platform built specifically for African research journals. We catalog peer-reviewed journals, compute impact factor scores, track citations, and provide researcher profile dashboards — all without paywalls.

items.q: Is AfriJournal Index free to use?
items.a: Yes. Browsing the catalog, searching journals, viewing rankings, and registering a researcher profile are all completely free. We offer a premium fast-track evaluation tier for publishers who want accelerated review within 48 hours. See our Pricing page for details.
AfriJournal Index is operated by Kenya Projects Organization (KENPRO), a Nairobi-based academic research and publishing organisation with decades of experience in African scholarly publishing.

The Platform indexes journals from all 54 African countries. Our regional AJIF score gives proportional weight to publication volume and open access availability within the continent, ensuring journals from smaller research ecosystems are fairly represented.

items.q: How do I submit a journal for indexing?
items.a: Navigate to the Submit page, complete the 2-step form with your journal details (name, ISSN, publisher, country, website URL), and submit. Our automated compliance engine will crawl your journal's website within minutes and generate a full evaluation report.

items.q: What does the automated compliance check evaluate?
items.a: Our crawl checks for: HTTPS encryption on your domain, homepage reachability, peer-review policy signals, editorial board listings, open access compliance markers, and publication frequency consistency.

Standard evaluation typically completes within 5–10 minutes for the automated crawl. The full editorial review may take up to 14 business days. Premium fast-track evaluation is completed within 48 hours.

items.q: Can I track my submission status?
items.a: Yes. After submitting, you will receive a unique submission ID. You can enter this ID (or your journal's ISSN) on the Submit status page to view real-time compliance logs and your current evaluation status.

items.q: How is the AJIF Impact Factor calculated?
items.a: The AJIF score combines a standard 2-year citation window score (aligned with global impact factor methodology) and a regional Africa-weighted score that accounts for open access publication volume within the continent. Full methodology is documented on our Methodology page.

The rankings leaderboard pulls live data from the database on every page load, so scores reflect the most current citation data available. Annual Impact Factor Reports are generated once per year for each indexed journal.

items.q: Can I filter the rankings by country?
items.a: Yes. The Rankings page includes a country filter that narrows the leaderboard to journals from any specific African country. You can also filter by discipline or quartile.

items.q: How do I create a researcher profile?
items.a: Register for an account on the Register page. Once registered and logged in, your profile is immediately accessible. As your articles are indexed into the platform, your h-index and citation metrics will update automatically.

Your h-index is computed using the standard definition: the largest number h such that h of your publications each have at least h citations. The calculation runs dynamically from your citation records in the database every time your profile is viewed.

items.q: What is ORCID and do I need one?
items.a: ORCID is a free, persistent digital identifier that distinguishes you from every other researcher. Providing your ORCID helps us automatically link your publications and verify authorship claims.
